title: Chonburi–Rayong–Chanthaburi 3-Day Coast Road Trip | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night driving plan along Thailand's eastern coast: Chonburi, Rayong and Chanthaburi. Start at Bang Saen and Ang Sila, pass Mae Ramphueng Beach, Ban Phe and Tung Prong Thong, finish at Noen Nang Phaya and Chanthaboon Riverside, with real timings you can follow.

h1:
Driving Thailand's Eastern Coast
Chonburi–Rayong–Chanthaburi, 3 Days 2 Nights
intro: This trip is a long, easy drive down Thailand's eastern coast. You start with seafood at Bang Saen and Ang Sila, roll past Rayong's Mae Ramphueng Beach and Ban Phe, then finish in Chanthaburi — a province with mangrove forest, the prettiest coastal scenic road in the region, and an old riverside quarter where people still actually live. We've laid it out as an unhurried 3 days and 2 nights. Driving yourself is by far the easiest way to do it, and each stop comes with rough times and distances so you can follow along.

blocks.html: The main route follows Sukhumvit Road heading east. It's about 1.5 hours from Bangkok to Bang Saen, another 1.5 hours from Bang Saen to Rayong, and roughly 1 hour 40 minutes from Rayong to Chanthaburi town. The prettiest stretch is Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, the seaside highway that runs unbroken from Rayong through Chanthaburi to Trat — over 100 km in total. Roll the windows down and cruise it all day.

This trip works best if you have a car, since several stops like Tung Prong Thong and Noen Nang Phaya have no public transport going right to them. If you'd rather not drive, you can hire a car with a driver by the day, but you'll be less flexible and the budget goes up.

items.note: Take the motorway or Sukhumvit and you'll reach Bang Saen around 10am. Leaving early means much lighter traffic.

Buy fresh seafood — prawns, squid, shellfish, crab — and there are stalls that'll cook it on the spot. Prices are easier on the wallet than at the beachfront. Stop to see the famous Ang Sila stone mortars while you're here.
Grab a seafront restaurant and order curry-fried crab, baby clams stir-fried with chilli jam, and deep-fried egg-stuffed squid to kick off the trip.

items.activity: Nong Mon Market for snacks and gifts
items.note: Sticky rice in bamboo (khao lam), khanom jak, the well-known hoi jor, and dried seafood — stock the car before heading south. Save the Chanthaburi gifts for the last day.

items.activity: Drive on into Rayong, check in near Mae Ramphueng Beach
items.note: Bang Saen to Rayong is about 1.5 hours. You can base yourself around Mae Ramphueng Beach or in town, whichever you prefer.

items.activity: Walk Ban Phe evening market and eat seafood
items.note: Ban Phe is the pier for boats to Koh Samet and Rayong's fresh seafood market. Wander and graze on grilled seafood, oysters and barbecued prawns.

blocks.title: On where to stay the first night
blocks.html: If you also want to fit in Koh Samet, stay in Ban Phe the first night and take the boat over for half a day — but that eats into the main trip a fair bit. This route focuses on hugging the mainland coast, so we've left Koh Samet for a separate trip.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Mae Ramphueng Beach–Tung Prong Thong–into Chanthaburi

items.activity: Morning stroll on Mae Ramphueng Beach
items.note: A sandy beach more than 10 km long, with a beachfront road that's great for a walk or a cycle in the morning breeze. Quiet, with good light for photos.

items.activity: Set off for Pak Nam Prasae
items.note: Drive along Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, about an hour from Rayong town. Sea views alternate with mangrove forest the whole way.

items.activity: Tung Prong Thong, Pak Nam Prasae
items.note: Walk the wooden boardwalk through the mangroves, where the golden-green prong thong trees stretch out in a wide field. Free entry. The late-morning sun is strong, so bring a hat and water.
An old fishing community with riverside seafood restaurants — try the fish noodle soup or river prawns. Stop to see HTMS Prasae, the navy ship moored as a memorial at the river mouth.

items.activity: Cross into Chanthaburi, Kung Krabaen Bay
items.note: The Kung Krabaen Bay Royal Development Study Center has a mangrove nature boardwalk. It's just before you reach Chanthaburi town.

items.activity: Noen Nang Phaya for evening views
items.note: A viewpoint over a curving coastal road that many call the prettiest in eastern Thailand. The soft late-afternoon light is best for photos.

items.activity: Check in to Chanthaburi town, find dinner
items.note: Staying in town makes it easy to get around on foot. Sleep in Chanthaburi tonight so you can explore the old quarter first thing tomorrow.

blocks.title: On the sun and the timing
blocks.html: Tung Prong Thong is comfortable to walk in the morning before 11am; after midday the sun is fierce and the boardwalk gets hot. Noen Nang Phaya, meanwhile, looks best in the evening. Splitting these two across different parts of the same day works out perfectly.

items.note: An old trading quarter along the Chanthaburi River, lined with old wooden houses where three religions live side by side. Walk and eat breakfast — Chanthaburi rice noodles (sen chan), local Thai sweets. The area has won a UNESCO conservation award.
The largest Catholic church in Thailand, across the river from the riverside community — cross the Niramon footbridge to reach it. Gothic architecture and beautiful stained glass.

items.activity: Tuk Daeng and Khuk Khi Kai, Laem Sing
items.note: Historic buildings from the period of the French occupation of Chanthaburi, at the Laem Sing river mouth, about 40 minutes from town. Worth a stop if you like history.

items.activity: Lunch around Laem Sing or Phlio Waterfall
items.note: Pick a seafood restaurant around Laem Sing, or drive straight on to Phlio Waterfall.

A waterfall inside the national park with clear, cool water year-round and a school of soro brook carp in the pool. It's a short walk in — a swim to cool off before the drive home. There's a park entry fee.

items.activity: Buy Chanthaburi gifts and head home
items.note: Durian in season, dried fruit, Chanthaburi pepper, dried seafood. Stop at a gift shop before getting on the road back to Bangkok.

blocks.text: Rough budget per person (3 days, 2 nights)

items: 2 nights' accommodation — around ฿1,200–3,000 per person sharing a twin room, depending on the standard of the stay
Fuel + tolls — around ฿1,500–2,200 per car for the Bangkok round trip; much cheaper per head if you split it among several people
Food — around ฿1,200–1,800 per person, with seafood as the main meals and cheaper market bites in between
Entry fees — Phlio Waterfall and the national park charge admission; Tung Prong Thong and Noen Nang Phaya are free. A few hundred baht per person all told.

blocks.text: Adjusting the plan to the time you have

items.name: Only 2 days, 1 night
items.blurb: Drop Bang Saen and head straight into Rayong. Day one: Mae Ramphueng Beach, Ban Phe, Tung Prong Thong, sleep in Chanthaburi. Day two: old quarter, Phlio Waterfall, then home.

items.name: Nature focus
items.blurb: Add more time at Kung Krabaen Bay and Phlio Waterfall, and trim the gifts and old quarter. Lean into the mangroves and the waterfall.

items.name: Seafood focus
items.blurb: Hit Ang Sila market, Ban Phe, Pak Nam Prasae and Chanthaburi's fresh market, with seafood for every main meal. The viewpoints become a bonus.

faq.q: How many days do you need for a Chonburi–Rayong–Chanthaburi trip?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just right if you want to fit in Bang Saen, Mae Ramphueng Beach, Tung Prong Thong, Noen Nang Phaya and Chanthaburi's old quarter without rushing. If you only have 2 days and 1 night, drop Bang Saen and start straight in Rayong.

faq.q: Can you do this route without your own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's much harder. Several stops like Tung Prong Thong and Noen Nang Phaya have no public transport going right to them. Your options are hiring a car with a driver by the day, or taking a coach into town and renting a motorbike to see just the in-town spots.

faq.q: What's the best time of year to go?
faq.a: November to February has the best weather — clear skies, calm sea. If you want to eat durian and Chanthaburi fruit, go April to June, but be ready for rain in the wet season.

faq.q: Are Noen Nang Phaya and Tung Prong Thong far apart?
faq.a: They're at different points along the coastal road. Tung Prong Thong is on the Pak Nam Prasae side in Rayong province, while Noen Nang Phaya is in Chanthaburi — you can drive from one to the other in a single day. We put Tung Prong Thong in the morning and Noen Nang Phaya in the evening because the light is best at different times.

faq.q: Is this trip suitable for kids or older travellers?
faq.a: Yes. It's a drive-and-stop trip with no hard walking, and most stops are easy on foot. Tung Prong Thong is a flat boardwalk and Phlio Waterfall is a short walk in. Choosing a hotel in Chanthaburi town makes it convenient to find food at night.
